name: Triangle-free graphs on 20 vertices whose every half is dense
description: construct() -> list of edges [u, v] of a simple triangle-free graph on vertices 0..19. The score is the minimum number of edges induced by any 10 of the vertices, computed over all 184756 subsets. Maximize; a score above 8 would disprove the Erdős-Rousseau conjecture for n = 20. For n = 20 the conjectured maximum of the score is 8, attained by the balanced C5 blow-up; a triangle-free graph with score 9 would be a counterexample.

sources.locator: Alexander A. Razborov, More about sparse halves in triangle-free graphs (2022). Crossref record inspected; Erdős Problem #128 ($250) page inspected: every n/2-set of a triangle-free graph is conjectured to span at most n^2/50 edges, tight for the C5 blow-up and the Petersen graph; proved with 1/50 replaced by 27/1024 by Razborov. For n = 20 the conjectured maximum of the score is 8, attained by the balanced C5 blow-up; a triangle-free graph with score 9 would be a counterexample.
Erdős Problem #128 (open (falsifiable, $250)); statement, history and current bounds reviewed 2026-09-24.
